title: General Physics II (Electricity and Magnetism)
description: The electricity and magnetism course, taught as PHY 104: Introductory Electricity and Magnetism before the CCMAS codes: electric charge and Coulomb's law, electric field and Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current, resistance and d.c. circuits, magnetic fields and forces, and electromagnetic induction with a.c. circuits. Built from Dr O. E. Oyewande's PHY 104 electricity lectures (2024) and P. O. Adesina's magnetism slides, with the CA tests labelled with the former code.

topics.title: Electric Charge and Coulomb's Law
topics.summary: Matter carries positive and negative charge, and a body is charged when its electrons and protons do not balance. Coulomb's law gives the force between point charges, and forces from several charges add as vectors.
subtopics: Positive and negative charge; conservation and quantisation
Coulomb's law and the constant k

topics.title: Electric Field and Gauss's Law
topics.summary: An electric field is the force per unit positive charge at a point, pictured with field lines. Fields of point charges and charge distributions add by superposition, and Gauss's law links the flux through a closed surface to the charge inside.

topics.title: Electric Potential
topics.summary: Electric potential is the work done per unit charge in bringing a test charge from infinity, a scalar measured in volts. Potential differences, equipotentials, the potential gradient and the potential energy of charge systems follow from it.
subtopics: Potential energy of a system of charges

topics.title: Capacitors and Dielectrics
topics.summary: A capacitor stores charge and energy on two conductors separated by an insulator. Its capacitance depends on its geometry and the dielectric, and capacitors combine in series and parallel.
subtopics: Capacitance C = Q/V and the farad
Capacitors in series and in parallel

topics.title: Current, Resistance and D.C. Circuits
topics.summary: Electric current is the flow of charge, driven by an e.m.f. and opposed by resistance. Ohm's law, resistivity, internal resistance, series and parallel combinations, power, Kirchhoff's laws and the Wheatstone bridge are used to analyse d.c. circuits.
subtopics: Current, drift velocity and current density
Kirchhoff's laws, Wheatstone bridge and potentiometer

topics.title: Magnetic Fields and Forces
topics.summary: Moving charges and currents produce magnetic fields and feel magnetic forces. The force on a charge is qv × B, so charges circle in uniform fields, and current-carrying wires feel forces used in motors and meters.
subtopics: Sources of magnetism and field lines
Force on a moving charge: F = qv × B
Circular motion; cyclotron and velocity selector
Torque on a coil; moving-coil instruments
Fields of wires and solenoids; forces between currents

topics.title: Electromagnetic Induction and A.C. Circuits
topics.summary: A changing magnetic flux induces an e.m.f., as described by Faraday's and Lenz's laws. Induction underlies generators and transformers, and alternating currents in resistors, inductors and capacitors are described by reactance and impedance.
subtopics: The a.c. generator; peak and r.m.s. values
Reactance, impedance and the RLC circuit
Resonance, power factor and the transformer
